item.title: China narrowing AI gap with US
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
China narrowing AI gap with US China's top artificial intelligence models have narrowed the performance gap with their United States' rivals to around 3 percent, the lowest on record, as advances by DeepSeek are increasingly matched by a wider group of Chinese developers. According to a report from Bloomberg Intelligence, the gap has fallen from about 9 percent in May and 15 percent earlier this year following the September release of DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash model. Bloomberg Intelligence senior analyst Robert Lea said that the speed of the catching-up process raises fresh questions over how long the US can maintain its technological lead, and could help Chinese AI firms capture a larger share of the global market. Notably, DeepSeek is no longer China's only serious challenger. Models developed by Alibaba, Moonshot AI and Z.ai — formerly known as Zhipu AI — are increasingly appearing near the top of global rankings. Artificial Analysis, a model-testing platform, has placed Alibaba's Qwen, Z.ai's GLM and Moonshot's Kimi models close to the frontier, with some scoring above DeepSeek on its own composite tests. Developers are increasingly using Chinese models. Over the 30 days through Wednesday, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash handled about 85 trillion tokens on model aggregation platform OpenRouter, making it the most-used model on the platform. Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash ranked third with about 55.2 trillion tokens, followed by Tencent's Hy4 Preview, while two models from Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi were also among the top 10. Zhang Yaqin, founding dean of Tsinghua University's Institute for AI Industry Research, said: "Before DeepSeek emerged, China was two to three years behind the US in large AI models. Since DeepSeek's breakthrough, the gap had narrowed to about two to three months, roughly the equivalent of a single model generation." Zhang said Chinese models — from DeepSeek and Alibaba's Qwen to ByteDance's Doubao — have entered the global top tier, while China is increasingly carving out its own path in areas such as model efficiency, open-source development and industrial applications. Yu Xiaohui, former president of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, said earlier in an interview, "Chinese models are now broadly comparable with leading overseas rivals in basic capabilities and can have an advantage in Chinese-language tasks." Stanford's 2026 AI Index said the performance gap between the top US and Chinese models had "effectively closed". As of March, the best US model was still ahead, but by only 2.7 percent, and models from the two countries had traded places at the top of rankings several times since early 2025. However, Yu also pointed to weaknesses in more demanding reasoning and tool use, and said China still lags behind the global frontier in original innovation. "China has built large amounts of computing capacity without yet turning all of it into the same kind of seamless ecosystem available to US developers. Domestic AI chips often use different software systems, forcing developers to spend more time adapting models to different hardware," he said. Tang Jie, a Tsinghua University computer science professor, said China still needs to catch up in high-end computing chips, fundamental AI architecture and the broader technology ecosystem, while producing more breakthroughs that originate in China rather than improving on existing approaches. chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: 10 things in China that blow foreign visitors' minds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
10 things in China that blow foreign visitors' minds Scanning a QR code to pay for breakfast, scrolling through videos even as the subway passes through tunnels — these are everyday routines that many Chinese people barely notice, yet many foreign visitors find hard to believe. Here are 10 things in China that amaze foreign visitors during their "China Travel" experiences. I. High-speed rail Many foreign visitors ride China's high-speed rail during their trips and often come away impressed. Beyond the speed, online ticketing, and digital tickets making travel easier — fares are affordable and the ride is smooth. By the end of 2025, China's high-speed rail network had exceeded 50,000 kilometers, more than the rest of the world combined, forming an "eight vertical, eight horizontal" grid that links cities, towns, and villages. II. High-speed rail stations Chongqing East Railway Station, built on the mountainous city's famously complex terrain, is the world's largest high-speed rail station built in a single phase. It covers about 1.22 million square meters, equivalent to 170 standard football fields, with 15 platforms and 29 tracks. It combines high-speed rail, subway, bus, taxi, and long-distance coach services in one transport hub. Engineers drove nearly 8,000 deep piles through complex karst geology to complete the project. III. Highways From the 18.5-kilometer-long Shanghai-Jiading Expressway — China's first expressway opened in 1988 — to a national expressway network of 199,400 km by the end of 2025, China has built one of the world's most extensive expressway systems in less than four decades. Across mountains, canyons, earthquake-prone areas, and permafrost regions, Chinese engineers have continued to turn difficult terrain into working transport links. Some key sections are even equipped with snow-melting and de-icing systems. IV. Micro electric vehicles Compact, economical, and well suited to dense urban environments, China's micro electric vehicles are notable for their affordability, with some models priced at only a few thousand US dollars. According to Reuters, the average price of a new car in the United States would be enough to buy five of China's best-selling affordable EV models. V. Modular housing China's prefabricated modular homes are drawing attention overseas for their low cost and fast assembly. Some three-bedroom units are priced at just over $10,000 and come with kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, and electrical fittings included. Built with high-strength steel structures, these homes are designed to withstand strong winds and earthquakes, with an estimated service life of about 20 years. VI. 5G networks China has built nearly 5 million 5G base stations, serving over 1.2 billion users, with coverage extending even to the summit of Mount Qomolangma. This infrastructure has enabled advances in remote education, telemedicine, and livestreamed agricultural commerce in rural areas. Börje Ekholm, CEO of Swedish telecom giant Ericsson, has warned that China has already deployed 5G standalone networks at scale, while Europe risks turning itself into a "museum" if it continues to lag behind in digital infrastructure. VII. Mobile payments Le Monde reported that coins and banknotes have become rare in everyday transactions in China, where mobile payments are widely used in markets, public transport, and daily consumer settings. NFC payments, digital transit cards, and palm-scan payment in selected transit and retail settings have made many purchases and commutes almost effortless. What looks like a simple tap or scan is backed by mobile networks, digital finance, and a fast-moving technology ecosystem. VIII. Public toilets Public restrooms have become an unexpected point of interest for foreign visitors. They are free of charge and widely available at airports, train stations, tourist attractions, and along city streets. Many are also equipped with accessible facilities and baby-care rooms, a notable contrast to the pay-per-use model still common in parts of Europe. IX. Drones Drone light shows have captivated foreign tourists. One visitor observed that in his home country, drones are associated with fear, while in China they light up the night sky. Beyond entertainment, drones played a critical role during this summer's flooding response in southern China's Guangxi Province, delivering emergency supplies, helping restore communications, and airlifting generators to affected areas. X. Public security Gallup's 2025 Global Safety Report found that 94 percent of Chinese residents said they felt safe walking alone at night, among the highest rates recorded worldwide. Foreign visitors have described walking on city streets alone late at night without fear, and one American traveler noted with surprise that convenience stores in China often operate unattended overnight. This sense of security is supported by public safety camera networks and community-level governance programs. What many foreign visitors find striking in China is not a single landmark or piece technology, but the way these things have been incorporated into daily life. The next thing that surprises the world may already be taking shape. The author is a commentator on international affairs. The views don't necessarily represent those of China Daily. If you have a specific expertise, or would like to share your thought about our stories, then send us your writings at opinion@chinadaily.com.cn, and comment@chinadaily.com.cn.

item.title: Record-breaking super El Nino intensifies in eastern Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Record-breaking super El Nino intensifies in eastern Pacific A super El Nino event with warming concentrated in the eastern Pacific officially formed in September, and is expected to become the strongest such event since systematic monitoring began, China's National Climate Center said. Sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific have been rising since May, pushing the Nino 3.4 index — a key indicator used to monitor the climate phenomenon — above the threshold for a super El Nino event, the center said. The index's three-month running average exceeded 2.5 C from July to September, reaching an average of 2.54 C over the period. In September, sea surface temperatures across much of the equatorial Pacific were above seasonal averages, with temperatures in the eastern Pacific's main warming zone more than 3 C above normal. The Nino 3.4 index reached 2.94 C, up 0.35 C from August. The center expects sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific to continue rising over the next three months, peaking in late autumn or early winter. El Nino is a recurring climate phenomenon characterized by unusually warm sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. It can alter atmospheric circulation patterns and influence weather conditions in many parts of the world, increasing the risk of certain extreme weather events.

item.title: China urges US to build stable cyberspace relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
China urges US to build stable cyberspace relations Beijing urged Washington on Friday to abandon double standards and political manipulation, and build peaceful and stable China-US relations in cyberspace based on mutual respect. Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning made the remarks after United States officials from the Justice Department said they seized seven internet domains that were "being used to help Chinese hackers scan and hack US and foreign critical infrastructure systems." China always opposes and takes legal action against hacking activities, she said, adding the country also firmly opposes the dissemination of false information and the creation of various disruptions for political purposes. Safeguarding cybersecurity is a shared concern of China and the US, Mao said, urging the US side to work with China to tackle cybersecurity risks through equal dialogue and negotiation.

item.title: Seeking new ways forward
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Seeking new ways forward Canada and EU edge closer as relations with US deteriorate over tariffs Ever since European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen suggested on Sept 16 that Canada considers becoming an "associate member" of the European Union, the two sides have worked rapidly to explore the possibility. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed the idea the following day, with both sides seemingly pushed together by the fact that they must diversify their partnerships because they can no longer fully rely on their traditional ally, the United States. On Oct 1, Canada and the European Commission held a new round of Digital Dialogue, with discussions including AI safety, regulation, and innovation. Meeting on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, US from Sept 30 to Oct 1, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu and EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic discussed deepening economic cooperation, with Sidhu highlighting critical minerals, defense, and digital trade as areas where Canada wants more collaboration with the EU. The two sides have already built close economic ties through the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, or CETA, which has been provisionally applied since 2017. Bilateral trade in goods and services reached 130 billion euros ($145.5 billion) in 2025, up 80 percent from 2016. A draft joint statement for the upcoming Canada-EU summit published by The Globe and Mail said the two sides planned to connect next-generation payment systems to enable faster, lower-cost cross-border transactions, while deepening cooperation in areas including critical minerals, digital trade, defense, and space. It added that the new partnership will be called an "Alliance for the Future". The developments echo von der Leyen's words in her State of the Union address, when she said: "We share one ocean, one set of values, one way of seeing the world." Carney struck a similar note in his address to the European Parliament the following day, saying: "An alliance for the future is a unique, positive approach that we will define together, building on our common strengths and based on shared values." The idea builds on years of deepening ties under CETA and gained momentum after the two sides established a Security and Defense Partnership in 2025. Achim Wambach, president of the ZEW-Leibniz Center for European Economic Research, said the alliance could become a blueprint for deep partnerships to secure vital resources and technologies. The Future of European Competitiveness report said that 70 percent of the European cloud and AI market is dominated by US hyperscalers. "The proposed closer partnership with Canada reflects the EU's broader 'de-risking' strategy to strengthen its strategic autonomy by reducing critical dependencies," Wambach said. The European Council's official page on EU-US relations notes that in 2025 the EU imported more than 82.9 billion cubic meters of liquefied natural gas from the US, equivalent to 26.4 percent of total EU gas imports and almost 58 percent of its LNG imports. In comparison, Canada provided 5,384 metric tons of natural uranium to EU utilities in 2025, accounting for 36.7 percent of total deliveries and making Canada the bloc's largest single source. Wambach pointed out that the EU's Critical Raw Materials framework, which includes partnerships with 16 countries, opens the door to more diversification. "Going beyond raw materials, the EU has potential to deepen partnerships with the Gulf region for energy and hydrogen, and India, Japan, and South Korea for advanced technologies and manufacturing," he said. Yan Xiaoxiao, an associate researcher at the Institute of International Relations at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, said a key factor pushing both the EU and Canada to diversify their partnerships is unstable policy from the US. "Canada has been hit by tariffs across sectors including steel, aluminum, autos, and a range of manufactured goods, while the EU agreed with Washington in 2025 to a 15 percent tariff ceiling on most of its exports," he said. "To diversify is important, practical, and beneficial for both sides." Huang Jing, a professor on American studies at Shanghai International Studies University, said the EU-Canada move was not the result of a long period of deliberation backed by corresponding policy and institutional preparations, but an improvised response to immediate pressures. "Whether it can develop into a deeper relationship depends not only on the domestic political constraints on both sides, but also on external factors, primarily the US," he said. Fabian Zuleeg, chief executive and chief economist of the Brussels-based European Policy Centre, said the added value of the proposed relationship would have to come from integration, rather than simply more cooperation. "CETA provides a strong trade framework, but an integrated partnership could go much further: closer integration of markets, finance, and supply chains, alongside economic security, defense procurement, technology, and critical raw materials. But deeper integration must come with obligations as well as benefits, including forms of alignment and sovereignty sharing," Zuleeg said. How far will the diversification go? Radhika Desai, a professor of political studies at the University of Manitoba in Canada, questioned how far such diversification can go, pointing both to Canada's heavy economic reliance on the US and to the institutional hurdles involved in closer integration with the EU. "Canada is so reliant on the United States that it's not going to lead to anything dramatically different," she said, adding that any much closer relationship with the EU would ultimately have to accommodate the interests of its 27 member states. She cited CETA as an example, saying 10 years after it was signed, the agreement is yet to secure ratification from 10 EU countries. Ryan Williams, a former member of Canada's House of Commons, said: "Europe already sells considerably more to Canada than Canada sells to Europe. Are we getting a new political relationship while Europe gets greater access to Canadian resources, defense contracts, investment opportunities, and potentially our market? Those aren't arguments against Europe. They're questions that should be answered before we create a category of EU relationship that has never existed before." According to a September report by independent advisory company Oxford Economics, total trade in goods and services between the EU and Canada has nearly doubled in value during the past three decades, partly thanks to CETA. However, that growth has been driven largely by Canadian imports from the EU, which has widened Canada's trade deficit with the bloc. The report also noted Canada's trade with the EU is roughly one-seventh of its trade with the US. Zuleeg said the arrangement could also have relevance beyond Canada, although not as a one-size-fits-all model. "It could provide a framework for deeper integration with like-minded partners such as the UK, Norway, Japan, or South Korea, potentially complemented by a broader Economic Security Alliance. The central challenge is institutional: how to enable meaningful participation without EU membership, while protecting EU decision-making and ensuring that partners remain genuinely like-minded. It should be flexible, differentiated, and capable of dealing with political divergence over time," he said. Desai argued that Canada should look beyond its traditional Western partners if diversification is its objective. "If you really wanted to diversify your trade relations, you would deepen your relations with China," she said. "Because practically everything that the United States has to offer, you can get from China. Practically everything you have been exporting to the United States, you can sell to China." Canada and the EU are expected to take the discussions further when Canada hosts their next summit in Montreal on Oct 29 and 30. Contact the writers at zhangzhouxiang@chinadaily.com.cn.

item.title: Gen Z finds a sweet future in hometown's green transition
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Gen Z returnee finds a sweet future in hometown's green transition At the southern foot of the Jinggang Mountains in Ji'an, Jiangxi province, the buzz of bees is becoming part of a new soundscape. Tianhe town once relied on coal mining as the backbone of the local economy. Today, as the town looks for greener ways forward, a young beekeeper is betting on an old family trade — with some new ideas of his own. Mao Yuanxiang, a Gen Z returnee, could have started his career in Shenzhen after graduating from university with a degree in cost engineering. Instead, he returned home. He chose beekeeping, an industry his family has been involved in for generations, and set about giving it a modern twist. Working with universities, Mao has introduced smart beehives and explored the development of honey-based drinks. He is also planning a bee-themed park where visitors can learn about beekeeping and the natural environment behind it. His story is part of a broader transformation taking place across Jinggangshan. Known as the cradle of the Chinese revolution, Jinggangshan is where Chinese revolutionaries explored a new path. The experience gave rise to the Jinggangshan Spirit, commonly described as a spirit of firm faith and hard work, seeking truth from facts and forging new paths, relying on the people and striving for victory. Tune in to the second episode of China Daily's documentary series Aspiration: One in a Hundred Million and follow reporter Yan An as she visits Tianhe town to meet Mao, a young Party member who is forging a new path back home. item.title: Strong demand in China boosts US exporters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Strong demand in China boosts US exporters Demand : Resilience of bilateral trade highlighted China's growing appetite for high-quality consumer goods and industrial inputs is drawing more products from the United States into its market, as holiday spending, industrial upgrading and the recent reciprocal tariff-cut arrangement offer US exporters more room to expand sales in the country, according to trade experts and business leaders. From fresh fruit and seafood to integrated circuits and energy products, US shipments to China have remained substantial, reflecting the complementary nature of the two economies and the potential for expanding imports to support more balanced and mutually beneficial bilateral trade, they said. The trend was particularly visible during the National Day holiday from Oct 1 to Wednesday, as stronger demand for food and other consumer products prompted Chinese importers to step up purchases from overseas suppliers. Oheng Supply Chain Management (Ningbo) Co, a cross-border food products importer based in Ningbo, Zhejiang province, imported 44.62 million yuan ($6.66 million) worth of products, including fresh cherries and fish oil from the US, in the first eight months of 2026. Ahead of the holiday, shipments of US fish oil, red yeast rice, fresh cherries and grapes purchased by the company arrived in China to replenish supplies for the holiday market. "The US is one of our main sources for products such as fish oil and cherries, with stable supply capacity," said Zhou Shouming, the company's director of customs affairs. "Judging from our sales, domestic consumers' demand for high-quality imported food continues to grow." In late September, China and the US released reciprocal tariff-cut lists covering about $30 billion worth of imports from each side. Zhou said the arrangement will lower costs for products including fresh cherries and grapes and give the company greater flexibility in pricing, allowing it to bring more high-quality US food products to Chinese buyers. Pistachios are also included on China's tariff-cut list. Nut growers in California are expected to export 111,000 metric tons of pistachios to China in the 2026 crop year (Sept 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027), according to Wonderful Pistachios & Almonds, the largest pistachio producer by production volume and sales revenue in the US. Anita Lam, managing director for China at Wonderful Pistachios, said the industry remains confident about the long-term growth potential for California pistachios in the Chinese market, adding that her company will continue to leverage its vertically integrated supply chain and long-standing operations to deepen its presence in the country. Demand for fresh seafood has also been strong in China. Imports of US lobsters through Ningbo Lishe International Airport were valued at 200 million yuan between January and August, surging 468.5 percent year-on-year, according to Ningbo Customs. Li Yongguo, president of Hengsheng Supply Chain (Dongguan) Co, a Dongguan, Guangdong province-based trading company, said that beyond food products, China's demand for imported integrated circuits has continued to grow, fueled by the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure and rising demand from the country's electronics manufacturing sector. The Chinese company imported 10.31 billion yuan worth of integrated circuits from the US in the first three quarters, up 74.2 percent year-on-year, statistics from Huangpu Customs in Guangdong showed. Miao Yingchun, a researcher at Wuhan University's Institute for International Studies in Wuhan, Hubei province, said China's demand for US products is being driven by both consumption and production — consumers seeking a wider range of quality goods and manufacturers requiring raw materials, components and equipment. Wang Huiyao, president of the Beijing-based think tank Center for China and Globalization, noted that the Chinese and US economies are deeply interconnected. "If the two countries can expand tariff reductions in specific areas and establish effective trade and investment mechanisms, even relatively limited steps at the outset could help strengthen confidence and pave the way for broader cooperation," he said. China-US trade rose 5.5 percent year-on-year to $400.84 billion during the January-to-August period, while China's imports from the US grew 3.4 percent year-on-year, data from the General Administration of Customs showed. The resilience of bilateral trade is also reflected in recent research. China's expanding import market continues to offer opportunities for US companies despite shifts in global trade and persistent bilateral economic tensions, according to a new report released in Los Angeles that examines changes in US exports to China and the broader impact of the China International Import Expo. The report, "The Evolution of the Structure of US Exports to China and the Extended Effects Index from a CIIE Perspective (2026)", was released earlier this week at the Bridge to Shanghai: Business Opportunities with China event, part of an overseas outreach series ahead of the ninth CIIE, which will be held in Shanghai from Nov 5 to 10. The report said the composition of trade also points to continuing economic complementarity between the world's two largest economies. It identifies China as the largest overseas market for US soybeans and cotton in 2026, and an important market for US integrated circuits and medical devices. It also said the US remains a major source of China's services imports and has maintained a surplus in bilateral services trade. Those patterns, according to the researchers, underscore the enduring commercial ties between the two economies even as tariffs, technology restrictions and changes in global sourcing have altered the bilateral trade landscape. Li Qingjuan, director of the Think Tank Center at Fudan University's Fudan International School of Finance, said the CIIE is no longer simply about bringing products into the Chinese market. Instead, it has evolved into a global platform for companies to showcase their products, connect with potential partners and explore business opportunities. Contact the writers at zhongnan@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Flame lit in Turin for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Flame lit in Turin for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade The flame for the 33rd Winter World University Games to be held in Changchun, northeastern China's Jilin province, was lit in Turin, Italy, on Thursday, marking another milestone in preparations for the event to be held early next year. At a ceremony held at the University of Turin, a torch from 1959, the year the first-ever Universiade was hosted by the city, was used to light the cauldron, from which the Changchun 2027 flame lantern was ignited. Gu Gang, mayor of Changchun, vice-chairman of the Organizing Committee for the 2027 Winter World University Games and chairman of its Executive Committee, handed the lantern to a flame bearer. The lantern was then carried through the streets of Turin. "Though thousands of miles apart, Changchun and Turin are now connected by the flame collection ceremony, united in youth and bound by sports," Gu said in an address. "With the flame as our bond and ice and snow as our medium, let's build a bridge of cultural exchange between East and West, bringing young people from all over the world closer together in mutual understanding and shared progress." "FISU stands for education, culture and sport, and Changchun is making every effort to provide an excellent mixture of these three elements," Leonz Eder, president of the International University Sports Federation, said. "The event will be a world-class sporting competition supported by excellent facilities, a high-quality international academic conference and cultural exchange programs that will allow students from around the world to experience the beauty of the province and the city, particularly its winter festival," he added. "Sports is a powerful way to bring people together," said Cristina Prandi, rector of the University of Turin, which has been home to the Universiade's permanent ceremonial cauldron, the "Flame of Knowledge", since 2018. "This is particularly important for us because participating in sports activities helps our international students connect with one another, and feel a part of the university community." Emanuele Ughetto, a local student who has studied Chinese for a long time and volunteered as a translator for the flame collection event, said that he was very happy to be picked for the ceremony. "I'm so excited to participate in such a grand event of transferring the flame to my motherland," said Yang Beishu, a Chinese conductor who lives in Turin. "The spirit of sports is a bond that links European people with Chinese people, as well as us overseas Chinese with our home," she said. The flame-lighting ceremony came a day after Changchun marked the 100-day countdown to the opening of the Games on Jan 15. With just over three months to go, Gao Jifeng, director of the Changchun Municipal Sports Bureau and deputy director of the Office of the Changchun 2027 Executive Committee, said preparations have entered the operational phase. Rather than building new competition venues, organizers have focused on upgrading existing facilities across the Changchun and Jilin competition zones, Gao said, adding that venue upgrades are now nearing completion, competition equipment is ready and schedules and lists of volunteers have been finalized. The flame will leave Turin and arrive in Changchun in mid-October. "In 99 days, student-athletes from around the world will gather in Changchun to challenge themselves and push their limits on ice and snow. May young people compete with courage and deepen their bonds through sport. May passion for sport cross all borders, dreams illuminate one another, and friendship endure for generations to come," said Gu. "We have seen the vibrant energy of Changchun, the warmth and hospitality of its people, and the truly remarkable progress achieved in such a short space of time. Let's meet in Changchun at its finest," said Eder, the president of FISU.
